post.summary: Enable or disable AML ongoing monitoring for users
post.description:
Turns AML ongoing monitoring on or off for the selected users, with the same semantics as the Business Console. Exactly one monitored AML screening is kept per user, so a profile that verified several times is monitored and billed once; disabling turns monitoring off across all of the profile's screenings. Users without any AML screening are screened first (billed as a regular AML screening) when they have the full name, date of birth and country needed; otherwise they are reported as `skipped_no_identity_data`.

Set `estimate_only: true` to preview counts and costs without writing anything. Selections of 20 profiles or fewer resolve inline and return `200` with the completed job; larger selections return `202` and run in the background - poll [Get AML monitoring job](#get-/v3/aml-monitoring/jobs/-job_id-/) with the returned `job_id`. Enabling is refused with `403` when the organization balance does not cover the estimate. Identifiers that match nothing are listed in `unmatched` and never fail the request: a selection that matches nothing completes as an empty job (`total` 0), the same convention as the batch delete endpoints.

schema.description: Select users with `vendor_data_list`, `didit_internal_id_list`, or both (the two lists are OR'd). At most 1000 identifiers per request across both lists.

is_enabled.description: true to enable monitoring, false to disable it.

estimate_only.description: When true, returns the cost estimate and performs no writes - no screening, no billing, no job.

vendor_data_list.description: Your own identifiers of the users to toggle, matched exactly as sent.

didit_internal_id_list.description: Didit internal ids of the users to toggle - the `didit_internal_id` returned by the create, get and list endpoints.

Disable.summary: Disable monitoring by Didit internal id

patch.summary: Update KYC data extracted from the ID document on a verification session
patch.description:
Correct the identity fields that were extracted (OCR / NFC) from the user's ID document — misread names, dates, document numbers, and so on — after the verification has finished. Typical callers are a compliance analyst working from your own back office, or an automated reconciliation job. Every field in the body is optional: only the keys you send are written, everything else is left untouched (`PATCH` semantics).

The session must belong to your application and be in `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, or `Kyc Expired` status. Sessions in any other state (e.g. still `In Progress`) return `404` with `"No Session matches the given query."` — distinct from the `"Not found."` returned for an unknown or deleted `sessionId`. The session must also carry an ID-verification (KYC) record: sessions whose workflow never ran an ID-verification step return `404` (`"The session does not have a KYC."`). For graph workflows with multiple ID-verification steps, target a specific step with `node_id` (query parameter or body field); when omitted, the most recent KYC record is patched.

Two derived fields are recomputed on every call: `full_name` (from `first_name` + `last_name`) and `issuing_state_name` (from `issuing_state`). If the free-text `address` changes, the server may also re-geocode it and refresh `parsed_address` (skipped for sandbox sessions). `extra_fields` and `parsed_address` are merged key-by-key rather than replaced — see the per-field descriptions for the `null`-to-delete semantics.

Submitting at least one valid field fires the `data.updated` [webhook](/integration/webhooks) (trigger `manual_review`) — even when the submitted values equal the stored ones. When values actually change, a `KYC_DATA_UPDATED` activity entry recording the changed fields with previous and new values is appended to the session's `reviews`, visible in [Get Decision](#get-/v3/session/-sessionId-/decision/) and the console activity timeline. The session's status and decision are **not** re-evaluated — use [Update Status](#patch-/v3/session/-sessionId-/update-status/) to change the outcome. An empty JSON body (`{}`) is accepted and simply returns the current KYC data without firing the webhook.

Accepts an API key or a console user token; either way the credential needs the `write:sessions` permission. Authentication and permission failures both return `403` — this API never responds `401`. Note that the session lookup runs before credential checks, so an unknown `sessionId` returns `404` even with missing credentials. This endpoint has a dedicated rate limit of 10 requests per minute per API key (invalid requests count too); the shared write budget of 300 requests per minute also applies.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: UUID of the User Verification (KYC) session whose extracted document data you are correcting. Business (KYB) session IDs are not valid here — for company data use [Update KYB Company Data](#patch-/v3/session/-sessionId-/kyb/-companyUuid-/update-data/).

parameters.name: node_id
parameters.description: Workflow graph node whose KYC record to patch, for graph workflows with multiple ID-verification steps (also accepted as a `node_id` body field). When omitted, the most recent KYC record on the session is patched. If no KYC exists for the given node, the call returns `404` (`"The session does not have a KYC for node '<node_id>'."`).

schema.description: All fields optional — send only what you want to change.

document_type.description: Document type code. Accepts the short codes listed in the enum, plus six long-form aliases normalized server-side before validation: `Passport` → `P`, `Identity Card` → `ID`, `Driver's License` → `DL`, `Residence Permit` → `RP`, `Health Insurance Card` → `HIC`, `Tax Card` → `TC`. Any other value (including `PASSPORT` in caps) returns `400`.

last_name.description: Family name(s). Also feeds the recomputed `full_name`.

gender.description: Sex as printed on the document: `M` (male), `F` (female), or `U` (unknown). Any other value — including `X` — returns `400`.

address.description: Free-text address as printed on the document. When this value changes (non-sandbox sessions only) and the structured address is still missing or incomplete, the server re-geocodes it synchronously before responding — the 200 body already reflects the refreshed `parsed_address`. The re-geocode also requires `issuing_state` to be present on the KYC record.

nationality.description: Nationality as printed on the document. Free text up to 32 characters — typically an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code (e.g. `ESP`), but not validated as one.

marital_status.description: Marital status where the document carries it. Any other value returns `400`.

extra_fields.description: Per-key overrides for document-specific extra fields (e.g. `blood_group`, `dl_categories`, `mrz_string`). Keys are merged into the existing override map: send a key with a value to set it, or with `null` / `""` to remove that key from the merged view. Send the whole field as `null` to clear all previously applied overrides. Must be a JSON object, otherwise `400`. The response always returns the merged view (OCR-extracted values with your overrides applied).

parsed_address.description: Structured address. Only these nested keys are accepted: `address_type`, `city`, `region`, `street_1`, `street_2`, `postal_code`, `country` — any other key returns `400`. Per-key semantics: a value sets the key, `null` removes it. `formatted_address` is recomputed server-side by joining `street_1`, `street_2`, `city`, `region`, `postal_code`, and `country` and is returned in the response — you cannot set it directly.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Lowercase input is normalized to uppercase; alpha-3 codes are rejected with `400`.

patch.description:
Set the status of a single verification feature (step) within a session **without changing the overall session decision**. Target the feature by its workflow graph `nodeId` (use `default` for non-graph workflows where the step has no node).

Works for both User Verification (KYC) and Business Verification (KYB) sessions and every step type — ID/OCR, Liveness, Face Match, NFC, AML, Proof of Address, Phone, Email, Database Validation, Questionnaire, and the KYB registry / documents / key-people checks.

`new_status` must be one of `Approved`, `Declined`, or `In Review`, and must differ from the feature's current status. A successful call fires a `data.updated` webhook and appends an activity entry (with actor attribution) to the session's review trail. This endpoint is **not** available for standalone API sessions (`session_type = API`).

Authenticate with your API key (`x-api-key`) or a user authorization header — either must carry the `write:sessions` privilege.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: Workflow graph node ID of the feature to update (for example `feature_ocr_1`). Use the literal value `default` for non-graph (single-step) workflows where the feature has no node ID.

new_status.description: Target status for this feature. Must differ from the current value.

comment.description: Optional free-text note recorded on the session's review trail for this feature change.

200.description: Feature status updated. Returns the targeted feature, its node ID, and the new status.

feature_type.description: Model name of the updated feature (e.g. `KYC`, `Face`, `FaceMatch`, `AML`, `POA`).

patch.description:
Set the review status of a **single AML hit** (a potential sanction / PEP / watchlist / adverse-media match) returned by AML screening, without changing the overall session decision. Identify the hit by its `hit_id` (the `id` of an entry in the AML check's `hits` array — see the session decision).

patch.summary: Update Proof of Address data extracted from the POA document on a verification session
patch.description:
Correct the fields extracted from the user's Proof of Address document — utility bill, bank statement, or other address evidence — after the verification has finished: issuer, dates, the printed name, the address itself, and banking details. Every field in the body is optional: only the keys you send are written, everything else is left untouched (`PATCH` semantics).

The session must belong to your application and be in `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, or `Kyc Expired` status. Sessions in any other state (e.g. still `In Progress`) return `404` with `"No Session matches the given query."` — distinct from the `"Not found."` returned for an unknown or deleted `sessionId`. The session must also carry a POA record: sessions whose workflow never ran a Proof of Address step return `404` (`"The session does not have a POA."`). For graph workflows with multiple POA steps, target a specific step with `node_id` (query parameter or body field); when omitted, the most recent POA record is patched.

`extra_fields` is merged key-by-key: nine known keys (`bank_iban`, `additional_names`, …) write through to dedicated POA columns, any other key is kept as a custom extra, and `null` / `""` deletes a key. `poa_parsed_address` accepts only the seven documented keys and recomputes `formatted_address` / `poa_formatted_address` after every edit. If the free-text `poa_address` changes, the server may also re-geocode it and refresh the structured address (skipped for sandbox sessions).

Unlike the KYC variant of this endpoint, the `data.updated` [webhook](/integration/webhooks) (trigger `manual_review`) fires only when at least one stored value **actually changed** — re-sending identical values is a silent no-op. When values change, a `POA_DATA_UPDATED` activity entry recording the changed fields with previous and new values is appended to the session's `reviews`, visible in [Get Decision](#get-/v3/session/-sessionId-/decision/) and the console activity timeline. The session's status and decision are **not** re-evaluated — use [Update Status](#patch-/v3/session/-sessionId-/update-status/) to change the outcome.

Accepts an API key or a console user token; either way the credential needs the `write:sessions` permission. Authentication and permission failures both return `403` — this API never responds `401`. Note that the session lookup runs before credential checks, so an unknown `sessionId` returns `404` even with missing credentials. This endpoint has a dedicated rate limit of 10 requests per minute per API key (invalid requests count too); the shared write budget of 300 requests per minute also applies.

An empty JSON body `{}` is a no-op: it returns `200` echoing the current POA record without firing the webhook (`has_changes` stays false).

parameters.description: UUID of the User Verification (KYC) session whose attached POA record you are correcting.

parameters.name: node_id
parameters.description: Workflow graph node whose POA record to patch, for graph workflows with multiple Proof of Address steps (also accepted as a `node_id` body field). When omitted, the most recent POA record on the session is patched. If no POA exists for the given node, the call returns `404` (`"The session does not have a POA for node '<node_id>'."`).

document_language.description: Language of the document, typically an ISO 639-1 code (e.g. `es`). Free text — not validated as a language code.

issuer.description: Organization that issued the document (utility company, bank, government agency).

poa_address.description: Free-text address as printed on the document. When this value changes (non-sandbox sessions only) and the structured address is still missing or incomplete, the server re-geocodes it in the background of the same request and may overwrite `poa_parsed_address` / `poa_formatted_address` with the geocoder result. The re-geocode also requires `issuing_state` to be present on the POA record.

extra_fields.description: Document-specific extras, merged key-by-key. Nine keys map to dedicated POA columns: `bank_account_number`, `bank_iban`, `bank_sort_code`, `bank_routing_number`, `bank_swift_bic`, `bank_branch_name`, `bank_branch_address`, `document_phone_number`, and `additional_names` (must be a list of strings or `null`, otherwise `400`). Any other key is stored as a custom extra field. Per-key semantics: a value sets the key; `null` or `""` deletes it. Must be a JSON object, otherwise `400`.

patch.summary: Update registry-extracted company data on a Business Verification (KYB) session
patch.description:
Correct the registry-extracted company data on a Business Verification (KYB) session — company name, registration number, addresses, status, contact details — identified by `companyUuid`. Typical callers are a compliance analyst fixing a registry misread, or your back office syncing corrected company data. Every field in the body is optional (`PATCH` semantics); an empty JSON body (`{}`) is a no-op that simply echoes the current company record.

Edits are written in two places at once: fields with a canonical company column (name, registration number, country, incorporation date, tax number, type, statuses, capital fields (`registered_capital`, `registered_capital_amount`, `registered_capital_currency`), alternative names, nature of business, website, email, phone, LEI, location, and `legal_address` → `registered_address`) update that column, and **every** submitted key is also merged into the `registry_data` snapshot (dates as ISO strings) so the "extracted from registry" view reflects the correction. Fields without a column — `region`, `registration_date`, `dissolution_date`, `control_scheme` — land in `registry_data` only. `user_provided_data` (what the end user confirmed in the hosted flow) is never touched, and `last_console_edit_at` is stamped on every non-empty PATCH.

Unlike the KYC/POA update endpoints, there is **no session-status gate**: the company can be edited at any point in the business session's lifecycle. The company must belong to the session in the path (`404` with `"KYB company does not belong to the given session."` otherwise) and to your application. Every non-empty PATCH fires the `data.updated` [webhook](/integration/webhooks) on the business session (trigger `console_registry_edit`) — even when the submitted values equal the stored ones. The session's status and decision are **not** re-evaluated, and no review/audit entry is recorded.

Accepts an API key or a console user token; either way the credential needs the `write:businesses` permission. Authentication and permission failures both return `403` — this API never responds `401`. Note that the session lookup runs before credential checks, so an unknown `sessionId` returns `404` even with missing credentials. The shared write budget of 300 requests per minute per API key applies.

For User Verification sessions, the KYC counterpart is `PATCH /v3/session/{sessionId}/update-data/`; to change the session decision itself use `PATCH /v3/session/{sessionId}/update-status/`.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: UUID of the parent Business Verification (KYB) session.

parameters.name: companyUuid
parameters.description: UUID of the company record to update (`registry_checks[].company.uuid` on the business session decision). Must belong to the session referenced by `sessionId`.

schema.description: All fields optional — send only what you want to change. Provided fields update the canonical company columns (where one exists) and are merged into the `registry_data` snapshot.

company_name.description: Legal name of the company. Written to the canonical column and the registry snapshot.

registration_number.description: Official registration number with the company registry.

country_code.description: Country of incorporation, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Case-insensitive (`us` is stored as `US`). Alpha-3 codes fail the 2-character limit with `400`.

region.description: Subdivision / region tag where the registry has one (e.g. US state). Stored in the registry snapshot only — it has no canonical column.

incorporation_date.description: Incorporation date in `YYYY-MM-DD`. Optional like every other field — the `PATCH` is partial. Any other date format returns `400`.

registration_date.description: Registration date where the registry distinguishes it from incorporation. Stored in the registry snapshot only.

dissolution_date.description: Dissolution date for companies that are no longer active. Stored in the registry snapshot only.

legal_address.description: Legal / registered address. Aliased server-side to the canonical `registered_address` column — the response returns it under `registered_address`, while the registry snapshot keeps the `legal_address` key you sent.

registry_status.description: Registry-reported company status. Lowercase, some values contain spaces (e.g. `struck off`, `no longer authorised`). Any other value returns `400`.

verification_status.description: Outcome of the registry verification. Any other value returns `400`.

alternative_names.description: Trade names, former legal names, DBA names (free text).

nature_of_business.description: Short description of the company's activity.

registered_capital.description: Human-readable registered capital (e.g. `USD 50000`). Use `registered_capital_amount` + `registered_capital_currency` for structured values, or this field for free-form text.

registered_capital_amount.description: Numeric registered-capital amount (up to 20 digits, 2 decimal places). Sets the `registered_capital_amount` column and is mirrored into `registry_data` as a decimal string; the response echoes it as a decimal string (e.g. `"1500000.50"`).

registered_capital_currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for `registered_capital_amount`. Case-insensitive (`usd` is stored as `USD`); values that are not exactly 3 letters return `400` with the ISO 4217 message. Sets the canonical `registered_capital_currency` column and is mirrored into `registry_data`.

website.description: Company website. Bare domains are accepted and normalized with an `https://` prefix (`docsprobe.example.com` is stored as `https://docsprobe.example.com`); values that still fail URL validation return `400`.

email.description: Contact email on file with the registry.

phone.description: Contact phone. Must match `+`, digits, spaces, dashes, dots, or parentheses, with 7-15 digits total — otherwise `400`.

legal_entity_identifier.description: LEI, where the company has one.

location_of_registration.description: City / subdivision of the registry of record.

vat_number.description: EU VAT number. Merged into the `registry_data` snapshot only — editing it here does not re-run VAT and tax ID validation, so `vat_validation_status` and the other `vat_*` result fields are unchanged.

control_scheme.description: Control / governance scheme when the registry exposes it. Stored in the registry snapshot only.

Single field.summary: Only the keys you send are written

No-op.summary: Empty body echoes the current record without firing the webhook

200.description: Company data updated (or echoed unchanged for an empty body). Returns the full KYB company record — the same shape as `registry_checks[].company` on the business session decision. Note how `legal_address` comes back as `registered_address`. `registered_capital_amount`/`registered_capital_currency` populate their canonical columns and are mirrored into `registry_data`.

schema.description: Full KYB company record — the same shape as the `company` object inside `registry_checks[]` on the business session decision.

node_id.description: Workflow graph node this company record belongs to, when the workflow is graph-based.

status.description: Feature lifecycle status of the registry check (e.g. `Not Finished`, `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`).

data_resolved.description: `true` when the company data is complete — always `true` for manual-entry companies; for registry-sourced companies, `true` once the registry fetch resolved.

registered_address.description: Canonical registered address — updated when you send `legal_address`.

is_from_registry.description: `true` when the company was pre-filled from a registry search rather than entered manually.

fetch_status.description: Registry fetch lifecycle for registry-sourced companies (`pending` / `resolved`); `null` for manual entries.

alternative_names.description: Alternative, trading, former or original-language company names as text, when reported.

registered_capital_amount.description: Canonical column. Returned as a decimal string (e.g. `"2750000.00"`).

registered_capital_currency.description: Canonical column. Set by the registry flow or by console/API edits via this endpoint.

vat_number.description: EU VAT number, when collected during the hosted registry step or edited afterwards.

vat_validation_status.description: Result of validating the VAT number or, when there is none, the `tax_number`, at registry submit. `valid` / `invalid`: decided by the official registry of the country (EU VIES, Norway, Switzerland, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Paraguay; Poland also by its domestic VAT register). `format_valid` / `invalid_format`: decided by the country's format and check-digit rules where no registry can be queried. `could_not_validate`: the registry was unavailable. `not_applicable`: no number, a country without registry or rules, or a sandbox session.

vat_validated_number.description: The number that was checked, as the source knows it (for example the VAT number derived from a French SIREN or a Dutch RSIN). `null` when no check ran.

vat_validation_source.description: The source that decided `vat_validation_status`: an official registry, or `format_rules`. `null` when no check ran.

vat_validated_name.description: Name registered with the source that validated the number, when it discloses one. Only set when the status is `valid`.

vat_validated_address.description: Address registered with the source that validated the number, when it discloses one. Only set when the status is `valid`.

vat_checked_at.description: Timestamp of the check. `null` when no check ran.

officers.description: Directors / officers attached to the company, including per-person KYC progress.

beneficial_owners.description: Beneficial owners attached to the company, including per-person KYC progress.

addresses.description: Registry address detail, when the registry returned any.

accounts.description: Registry filing dates, when available. Annual returns and general meetings use last_annual_return_date and last_agm_date; they are distinct from financial accounts.

registry_data.description: Raw registry payload snapshot. Every key you PATCH is merged into this map (dates serialized as ISO strings), so the "extracted from registry" view reflects operator corrections.

user_provided_data.description: What the end user typed during the hosted registry-confirmation step. Never modified by this endpoint.

confirmed_by_user_at.description: When the end user confirmed the company data in the hosted flow.

last_console_edit_at.description: Stamped on every successful non-empty PATCH, so UIs can surface "edited by operator" context.

patch.summary: Skip (or re-require) a Key People party on a Business Verification (KYB) session
patch.description:
Exempt a Key People party from verification, or put it back in scope. This is the operator escape hatch for a party that can never finish its own check - most often because the individual KYC session handed to a UBO or director was deleted, which freezes that child's status and leaves the KYB parked in `Awaiting User` with nothing left that could move it.

Setting `is_skipped: true` drops the party out of the Key People aggregation and immediately recomputes the `KYBKeyPeopleCheck` and the parent session status, so the business session can settle and then be approved or declined. Sending `is_skipped: false` puts the party back in scope and the check goes back to waiting on it.

Unlike the applicant-facing skip in the hosted Key People screen, this endpoint is **not** gated by the role's `allow_skip` setting - that flag limits what the applicant may decide, not what your analyst may override. `requires_verification` is deliberately left untouched, so an overridden party reads as `requires_verification: true` **and** `is_skipped: true` and the record still shows what the rules asked for.

The party must belong to the session in the path (`404` with `"Party does not belong to the given session."` otherwise) and to your application. A PATCH that actually changes the flag fires the `data.updated` [webhook](/integration/webhooks) on the business session with trigger `console_key_people_skip`; a PATCH that sets the flag to its current value is a no-op that echoes the party back.

Accepts an API key or a console user token; either way the credential needs the `write:businesses` permission.

parameters.description: UUID of the parent Business Verification (KYB) session.

parameters.name: partyUuid
parameters.description: UUID of the Key People party to update (`key_people_checks[].submitted.parties[].uuid` on the business session decision). Must belong to the session referenced by `sessionId`.

is_skipped.description: `true` exempts the party from verification so the Key People check can settle without it; `false` puts it back in scope.

200.description: Party updated (or echoed unchanged when the flag already had this value). Returns the party - the same shape as an entry of `key_people_checks[].submitted.parties[]` on the business session decision.

schema.description: Key People party record - the same shape as an entry of `key_people_checks[].submitted.parties[]` on the business session decision.

entity_type.description: Whether the party is an individual or a company.

is_skipped.description: Whether the party is exempt from verification.

requires_verification.description: What the role and threshold rules asked for. Left untouched by this endpoint.

kyc_session_status.description: Status of the linked individual KYC session, frozen at deletion time when the session was deleted.

kyc_session_url.description: Link to the linked individual KYC session. `null` when there is none or when it was deleted.

kyc_session_deleted.description: The linked individual KYC session was deleted, so it can never settle.

400.description: Validation error on the request body. `is_skipped` is the only field this endpoint reads, and it is required. Field errors arrive as `{"<field>": ["<message>"]}`. Body validation runs *after* the party lookup, so a malformed `is_skipped` sent to a party that does not exist reports `404`, not `400`.

Non-boolean is_skipped.summary: Value is not a boolean — `"maybe"`, `2`, `[]`. Booleans plus `"true"`/`"false"`, `1`/`0` and `"yes"`/`"no"` are all accepted

is_skipped: This field may not be null.

You do not have permission to perform this action.

Credential and permission checks run before the party lookup, so an unauthorised call reports `403` rather than `404`. There is no separate session lookup: an unknown `sessionId` paired with a party of yours reports the mismatch message.

value.detail: Not found.

value.detail: Party does not belong to the given session.

delete.description:
An opted-in application keeps one separately managed, image-free face biometric template anchored to the User when a session is deleted (see `DELETE /v3/session/{sessionId}/delete/`). Templates are biometric data with a finite `expires_at`; they never contain images, session data, or identity fields, and they are purged on User deletion, privacy erasure, expiry, or an explicit purge. These endpoints accept application API keys (`x-api-key`) only; Business Console user tokens are rejected with `403`.

Purges one template: it is removed from every kind of matching and the stored template is deleted. Irreversible and recorded on the audit trail with the acting principal.

**Retry semantics:** Didit deletes the stored template first and only then marks the template purged. If a biometric store is unavailable the call returns `503`, the template moves to `status: purge_failed` and is already excluded from matching; repeat the same call to finish. Repeating a purge of an already purged template returns `already_purged`.

Templates are also purged by `POST /v3/users/delete/` for the owning User, by any deletion of that User's sessions with `deletion_instruction: privacy_erasure`, and automatically at `expires_at`.

parameters.name: template_uuid
parameters.description: Template id, as returned in `biometric_template_uuid` by the session deletion endpoints, `biometric_template_id` on a Face Search match, or the list endpoint.

403.description: Console user token, or the API key is not allowed. These endpoints accept application API keys only.

value.detail: You do not have permission to perform this action.

404.description: Unknown template, a template of another application, or (on `GET`) a purged template.

value.detail: Biometric template not found.

503.description: A biometric store was unavailable while retaining or purging a biometric template. Nothing is deleted; repeat the same request. Retries are idempotent and converge on a single template.

value.detail: The biometric-template operation could not finish because an external store is unavailable. The operation is retryable.

An opted-in application keeps one separately managed, image-free face biometric template anchored to the User when a session is deleted (see `DELETE /v3/session/{sessionId}/delete/`). Templates are biometric data with a finite `expires_at`; they never contain images, session data, or identity fields, and they are purged on User deletion, privacy erasure, expiry, or an explicit purge. These endpoints accept application API keys (`x-api-key`) only; Business Console user tokens are rejected with `403`.

Purges many templates in one call, by explicit id list or with `delete_all: true` optionally narrowed by the same filters as the list endpoint. Templates are purged one by one and each result reports `purged` or `already_purged`. If a biometric store is unavailable the call returns `503` at the first failing template: templates purged earlier in the request stay purged, the failing one moves to `purge_failed` (already excluded from matching), and repeating the request finishes the job.

post.description:
Retrieve the Lite profile **plus the direct shareholders** (natural persons and corporate entities, with their ownership bands) of one candidate returned by `POST /v3/kyb/search/`.

**Pairing with search.** Pass the candidate's `kyb_response_id` exactly as returned by a search of the same application. The search runs on the Lite registry chain; when the country's ownership data lives at another registry Didit re-finds the company there by registration number, at no extra cost.

**Billing.** Billed at the country's Shareholders price - see [KYB registry pricing](/getting-started/kyb-registry-pricing). When the registry holds no shareholder record for the company (or the country offers no ownership data at all) the Lite profile is delivered and billed instead: read `registry_tier_delivered` and `registry_ownership_status`. The balance is checked against the Shareholders price before any registry call (`403` when short).

**Availability.** v3 only. Every call creates a business session (its id is the `request_id`).

**Pending reports.** When a report is still being prepared, or the ownership section has not been retrieved from the registry yet, the endpoint returns 202 Accepted, kyb_registry.fetch_status=pending, kyb_registry.registry_ownership_status=pending, and registry_tier_delivered=null. Keep request_id and retrieve GET /v3/session/{request_id}/decision/ until registry_checks[0].company.fetch_status is resolved. Didit completes the report automatically and charges the delivered tier once it is ready. Do not repeat the purchase while it is pending; every new POST creates a separate request.

kyb_response_id.description: Candidate handle from `POST /v3/kyb/search/` (`kyb_registry.companies[].kyb_response_id`). Ephemeral — use it shortly after the search that produced it.

vendor_data.description: Your identifier for this company; echoed back and stored with the business session.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON stored with the business session and echoed back.

save_api_request.description: Must be `true` (the default). KYB registry selects are always persisted so billing and retrieval can be tracked; `false` returns `400`.

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import os, time, requests

search = requests.post(
    "https://verification.didit.me/v3/kyb/search/",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["DIDIT_API_KEY"]},
    json={"country_code": "GB", "name": "Tesco"},
    timeout=60,
).json()
kyb_response_id = search["kyb_registry"]["companies"][0]["kyb_response_id"]

resp = requests.post(
    "https://verification.didit.me/v3/kyb/shareholders/",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["DIDIT_API_KEY"]},
    json={"kyb_response_id": kyb_response_id, "vendor_data": "company-1234"},
    timeout=90,
)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()
request_id = data["request_id"]
print("Keep this request ID:", request_id)
company = data["kyb_registry"]
if resp.status_code == 202 or company.get("fetch_status") == "pending":
    # This client wait limit does not cancel the report or create a new purchase.
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 300
    while company.get("fetch_status") != "resolved" and time.monotonic() < deadline:
        time.sleep(5)
        decision = requests.get(
            f"https://verification.didit.me/v3/session/{request_id}/decision/",
            headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["DIDIT_API_KEY"]},
            timeout=30,
        )
        decision.raise_for_status()
        checks = decision.json().get("registry_checks") or []
        if checks:
            company = checks[0].get("company") or company
if company.get("fetch_status") == "resolved":
    print(company["company_name"], company["registry_tier_delivered"])
else:
    print("Still processing; retrieve this request later:", request_id)

        checks = decision.json().get("registry_checks") or []
        if checks:

if company.get("fetch_status") == "resolved":

import os
import requests

headers = {
    "x-api-key": os.environ["DIDIT_API_KEY"],
    "Idempotency-Key": "your-unique-attempt-key"
}
payload = {'country': 'FIN',
 'vendor_data': 'your-customer-reference',
 'metadata': {'reference': 'example'},
 'return_url': 'https://app.example.com/identity/complete'}

response = requests.post(
    "https://verification.didit.me/v3/id-verification/wallets/ftn/",
    headers=headers,
    json=payload,
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json())

post.description: Start a Personalausweis sign-in (Bundesministerium des Innern (eID); DEU) without any workflow. Billed once, only when the identity is verified. The response carries next_action.type=redirect with the URL to send the user's browser to; the user returns to return_url with request_id and result appended. Read the outcome with GET /v3/id-verification/wallets/verifications/{request_id}/ or from the webhook, never from the URL. Sandbox applications get a deterministic simulation (simulated: true) that never contacts the provider.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional retry-safety key (max 255 characters). Retrying with the same key, wallet and body returns the original verification without starting a second sign-in; the same key with another wallet or body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused.

400.description: Field validation errors ({field: [messages]}), or error return_url_invalid, return_url_not_allowed, invalid_personal_code, invalid_phone_number or idempotency_key_invalid.

403.description: Missing or invalid credentials ({detail}), or error wallet_unavailable, insufficient_credits or contract_rate_missing.

502.description: error wallet_provider_unavailable: the provider could not start; nothing was created.

503.description: error wallet_not_configured: this environment cannot reach the wallet.

post.description:
Render the email that would accompany a KYC or KYB resubmission without changing the session, resetting checks, extending its expiry, running checks or sending mail. Requires write:sessions and an application-scoped session in Approved, Declined, In Review, Kyc Expired or Abandoned status. The server validates the selected workflow steps and renders its fixed translated template with the applicable verified white-label sender and branding. The request cannot set a subject, message body or action URL.

The response includes the recipient, sender, subject, HTML, resolved steps and a signed preview_token. requires_user_action describes whether the selected steps include an interactive check. Email delivery remains conditional: if automatic checks finalize the verification during the subsequent resubmission, no action-request email is sent.

This preview does not reserve session state or authorize delivery. After reviewing it, call Update Session Status with new_status=Resubmitted, the same selection, recipient and language, and email_preview_token set to the returned preview_token. The receipt expires after 15 minutes. When a receipt is supplied, changed inputs, message content, sender or session state return 409 before any mutation or send. Existing integrations may omit the receipt. Regenerate the preview after a conflict. Treat the response as sensitive verification content; responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Render HTML in a sandboxed frame, never directly in your application DOM.

request_id.description: Session id of the verification. A `Retry` send returns the same `request_id` as the original send. This id appears in the Business Console, is returned again by a finalized `POST /v3/phone/check/`, and can be passed to `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/`.

status.description: `Success` — OTP sent to a new verification. `Retry` — OTP re-sent for the pending verification created by a previous send. `Blocked` — the anti-fraud layer refused to send; the verification is immediately finalized as `Declined` and nothing is billed.

reason.description: Why a send was `Blocked` (e.g., `repeated_attempts`, `suspicious`, `spam`). `null` on `Success` and `Retry`.

vendor_data.description: Echo of the `vendor_data` stored on the session (from the first send).

metadata.description: Echo of the `metadata` stored on the session (from the first send).

request_id.description: On `Approved`/`Declined`: the session id of the matched verification — identical to the `request_id` returned by `POST /v3/phone/send/`. On `Failed` and `Expired or Not Found`: a random one-off UUID that cannot be looked up later.

status.description: `Approved` — correct code, no declining risk. `Declined` — terminal: a declining risk matched or the attempt budget (3) was exhausted. `Failed` — wrong code, attempts remaining. `Expired or Not Found` — no pending verification for this number in the last 5 minutes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the outcome, including the number of attempts remaining after a wrong code.

phone.description: Full phone report. Present (non-null) only on finalized outcomes (`Approved`/`Declined`); `null` on `Failed` and absent on `Expired or Not Found`.

status.description: Final status of the phone verification. Matches the top-level `status` for finalized checks.

phone_number.description: National number without the country calling code.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the number.

carrier.description: Current network serving the number, from the carrier lookup run at finalization.

name.description: Carrier name. Empty string when the lookup could not identify it.

type.description: Line type reported by the lookup: `mobile`, `fixed_line`, `voip`, `isp`, `vpn`, `toll_free`, `premium_rate`, `pager`, `payphone`, `satellite`, `service`, `shared_cost`, `short_codes_commercial`, `calling_cards`, `local_rate`, `universal_access`, `voice_mail`, `other`, or `unknown`.

is_disposable.description: `true` when the number belongs to a temporary/burner number service.

is_virtual.description: `true` when the line type is virtual (`voip`, `isp`, or `vpn`).

verification_method.description: Channel that actually delivered the OTP once delivery is confirmed (e.g., `whatsapp`, `sms`); until then, the requested channel.

verification_attempts.description: Number of OTP sends for this verification (1, or 2 after a retry).

verified_at.description: When the correct code was entered. `null` if the verification was never approved.

warnings.description: Risk warnings recorded during the verification (duplicate, disposable, VoIP, attempts exceeded, blocklist, etc.). Empty array when there are none.

feature.description: Feature that produced the warning. Always `PHONE` here.

additional_data.description: Risk-specific context (e.g., the duplicated session id for duplicate risks). `null` when the risk carries no extra data.

log_type.description: Severity. `error` risks decline the verification, `warning` flags it for review, `information` is recorded without affecting the status.

short_description.description: Human-readable one-line summary of the risk.

lifecycle.description: Chronological audit trail of the verification. Event `type` is one of `PHONE_VERIFICATION_MESSAGE_SENT`, `PHONE_VERIFICATION_RETRY_MESSAGE_SENT`, `PHONE_VERIFICATION_BLOCKED`, `PHONE_DELIVERY_DELIVERED`, `PHONE_DELIVERY_UNDELIVERABLE`, `VALID_CODE_ENTERED`, `INVALID_CODE_ENTERED`, `PHONE_VERIFICATION_APPROVED`, `PHONE_VERIFICATION_DECLINED`, `PHONE_VERIFICATION_IN_REVIEW`, `PHONE_VERIFICATION_EXPIRED`.

details.description: Event-specific payload. Send events: `{status, reason, channel, actual_channel}` (`actual_channel` is filled once delivery is confirmed). Delivery events: `{channel, status}`. Code-entry events: `{code_tried, status}`. Final-status events: `null`, or `{reason}` when declined or in review.

fee.description: USD amount billed for this event. Non-zero only on send events (the delivery price); 0 for code entries, delivery confirmations, and status events.

matches.description: Other sessions of your application (KYC, KYB, or API) where the same phone number was used by a different user (different `vendor_data`). Up to 5 entries, a synthetic list-entry blocklist match first when present (session-derived matches keep query order). Empty array when there are no matches.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of that session.

status.description: Status of that session (e.g., `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Progress`).

is_blocklisted.description: Whether the phone number is on your application's blocklist.

api_service.description: For API-type sessions, the standalone API that created it (e.g., `PHONE_VERIFICATION`); `null` for regular verification sessions.

source.description: Where the match was found. Usually `session`; a blocklist hit via an organization list entry prepends a synthetic match with `source: "list_entry"` and null `session_id`/`session_number`.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of the matched verification's session. `null` on `Expired or Not Found`.

metadata.description: `metadata` of the matched verification's session. `null` on `Expired or Not Found`.

created_at.description: Timestamp of this check response.

request_id.description: Session id of the verification. A `Retry` send returns the same `request_id` as the original send. This id appears in the Business Console, is returned again by a finalized `POST /v3/email/check/`, and can be passed to `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/`.

status.description: `Success` — OTP emailed to a new verification (billed). `Retry` — fresh OTP emailed for the pending verification created by a previous send (free). `Undeliverable` — the address failed deliverability validation or the message could not be sent; the verification is immediately finalized as `Declined` and nothing is billed.

vendor_data.description: Echo of the `vendor_data` stored on the session (from the first send).

metadata.description: Echo of the `metadata` stored on the session (from the first send).

request_id.description: On `Approved`/`Declined`: the session id of the matched verification — identical to the `request_id` returned by `POST /v3/email/send/`. On `Failed` and `Expired or Not Found`: a random one-off UUID that cannot be looked up later.

status.description: `Approved` — correct code, no declining risk. `Declined` — terminal: a declining risk matched or the attempt budget (3) was exhausted. `Failed` — wrong code, attempts remaining. `Expired or Not Found` — no pending verification for this address in the last 5 minutes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the outcome, including the number of attempts remaining after a wrong code.

email.description: Full email report. Present (non-null) only on finalized outcomes (`Approved`/`Declined`); `null` on `Failed` and absent on `Expired or Not Found`.

status.description: Final status of the email verification. Matches the top-level `status` for finalized checks.

is_breached.description: `true` when the address appears in known data breaches (breach intelligence lookup run at finalization).

breaches.description: Up to 5 most recent known breaches containing this address. Empty array (or omitted) when `is_breached` is `false`.

breach_emails_count.description: Total number of accounts exposed in the breach.

description.description: Human-readable description of the breach (may contain HTML markup).

logo_path.description: URL of the breached service's logo.

data_classes.description: Categories of data exposed, in snake_case (e.g., `email_addresses`, `passwords`).

is_verified.description: Whether the breach has been verified as legitimate.

is_disposable.description: `true` when the domain belongs to a known disposable/temporary-mail provider.

is_undeliverable.description: `true` when the address cannot receive mail (failed syntax or DNS/MX validation, or the message bounced).

verification_attempts.description: Number of OTP sends for this verification (1, or 2 after a retry).

verified_at.description: When the correct code was entered. `null` if the verification was never approved.

warnings.description: Risk warnings recorded during the verification (duplicate, breached, disposable, undeliverable, attempts exceeded, blocklist, etc.). Empty array when there are none.

feature.description: Feature that produced the warning. Always `EMAIL` here.

additional_data.description: Risk-specific context (e.g., the duplicated session id for duplicate risks). `null` when the risk carries no extra data.

log_type.description: Severity. `error` risks decline the verification, `warning` flags it for review, `information` is recorded without affecting the status.

short_description.description: Human-readable one-line summary of the risk.

lifecycle.description: Chronological audit trail of the verification. Event `type` is one of `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_MESSAGE_SENT`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_RETRY_MESSAGE_SENT`, `VALID_CODE_ENTERED`, `INVALID_CODE_ENTERED`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_APPROVED`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_DECLINED`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_IN_REVIEW`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_EXPIRED`.

details.description: Event-specific payload. Send events: `{status, reason}`. Code-entry events: `{code_tried, status}`. Final-status events: `null`, or `{reason}` when declined or in review.

fee.description: USD amount billed for this event. Non-zero only on the first successful send; 0 for retries, code entries, and status events.

matches.description: Other sessions of your application (KYC, KYB, or API) where the same email address was used by a different user (different `vendor_data`). Up to 5 entries; a synthetic list-entry blocklist match is prepended when present (and only when no session-derived blocklisted email exists) — session-derived matches keep created_at order. Empty array when there are no matches.

session_id.description: Session id of the other verification that used this email address.

session_number.description: Human-friendly sequential number of that session.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of that session.

status.description: Status of that session (e.g., `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Progress`).

is_blocklisted.description: Whether the email address is on your application's blocklist.

api_service.description: For API-type sessions, the standalone API that created it (e.g., `PHONE_VERIFICATION`); `null` for regular verification sessions.

source.description: Where the match was found. Usually `session`; a blocklist hit via an organization list entry prepends a synthetic match with `source: "list_entry"` and null `session_id`/`session_number`.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of the matched verification's session. `null` on `Expired or Not Found`.

metadata.description: `metadata` of the matched verification's session. `null` on `Expired or Not Found`.

created_at.description: Timestamp of this check response.

WorkflowListItem.description: One workflow version in the list view.

uuid.description: Per-version UUID. Use as `{settings_uuid}` for get/update/delete, and as `workflow_id` when creating sessions.

workflow_id.description: Stable group ID shared by every version of the same workflow. Equals `uuid` for version 1.

workflow_type.description: Base type for simple workflows: `kyc`, `kyb`, `adaptive_age_verification`, `biometric_authentication`, etc. `null` for graph-based workflows without a KYB feature.

is_default.description: Whether this is the default workflow for new sessions.

is_white_label_enabled.description: Whether white-label customization applies to sessions created with this workflow.

total_price.description: Fixed price per verification in USD (JSON number, excludes variable-priced features such as DATABASE_VALIDATION and PHONE_VERIFICATION).

min_price.description: Cheapest fixed price across workflow-graph paths, in USD.

max_price.description: Most expensive fixed price across workflow-graph paths, in USD.

features.description: Enabled features as a single `" + "`-joined string, e.g. `"OCR + LIVENESS + FACE_MATCH"`. Split on `" + "` to get a list.

is_simple_workflow.description: True when the workflow has no custom workflow graph.

is_editable.description: True when this version is a `draft` (drafts are editable in place; published versions are immutable in the Console).

workflow_url.description: Public shareable verification URL for this workflow (`https://verify.didit.me/u/<token>`).

max_retry_attempts.description: Maximum retry attempts allowed after a declined verification (0-10).

retry_window_days.description: Rolling window in days used to count retries (1-365). `null` = all-time limit.

session_expiration_time.description: Seconds before an unfinished session expires (3600-2419200).

version.description: Version number within the `workflow_id` group, starting at 1.

status.description: Version status. New sessions use the latest `published` version of a group.

has_draft.description: True when any version in this `workflow_id` group is currently a draft.

created_by.description: Who created this version: `{name, email, type}` where `type` is `user` (Console user, `email` set) or `api_key` (`name` is the client id, `email` is null). `null` when no creator was recorded.

SimpleWorkflowRequest.description: Create a simple linear workflow. The API converts this feature list into a node-based workflow graph internally. STRICT field whitelist: any key not listed here (including `workflow_type`) is rejected with a 400.

workflow_label.description: Display name for the workflow (max 50 characters). Defaults to `"ID Verification"` when omitted — always set it so workflows stay distinguishable.

is_default.description: Set this workflow as the default for new sessions.

status.description: Omit this field to create a published workflow ready for sessions. Use `draft` only when you want to save without publishing.

features.description: Verification features in execution order. The API links each item to the next one and adds one final status node automatically.

is_white_label_enabled.description: Enable white-label customization for sessions created with this workflow.

is_desktop_allowed.description: Allow the verification flow to run on desktop browsers.

max_retry_attempts.description: Maximum retry attempts allowed after a declined verification. `0` blocks the user after the first decline.

retry_window_days.description: Rolling window in days used to count retries. `null` enforces an all-time limit.

face_liveness_max_attempts.description: Maximum liveness submissions per session. Default 3: one initial attempt plus two retries. This value is also copied into generated liveness and age-estimation workflow nodes unless the feature-level config overrides it.

face_match_max_attempts.description: Maximum face-match submissions per session. Default 3: one initial attempt plus two retries. This value is also copied into generated face-match workflow nodes unless the feature-level config overrides it.

session_expiration_time.description: Seconds before an unfinished session expires. Minimum 1 hour (3600), maximum 4 weeks (2419200).

SimpleWorkflowUpdateRequest.description: Update workflow metadata or replace the full linear feature list. STRICT field whitelist: any key not listed here is rejected with a 400.

workflow_label.description: Display name for the workflow (max 50 characters).

is_default.description: Set this workflow as the default for new sessions.

status.description: Controls versioning. Omit to update the current version in place (drafts auto-publish). `published` on an already-published version creates and returns a NEW version. `draft` is only valid while the version is still a draft.

features.description: If provided, this replaces the full feature order and configuration.

is_white_label_enabled.description: Enable white-label customization for sessions created with this workflow.

is_desktop_allowed.description: Allow the verification flow to run on desktop browsers.

max_retry_attempts.description: Maximum retry attempts allowed after a declined verification. `0` blocks the user after the first decline.

retry_window_days.description: Rolling window in days used to count retries. `null` enforces an all-time limit.

face_liveness_max_attempts.description: Maximum liveness submissions per session. This value is also copied into generated liveness and age-estimation workflow nodes unless the feature-level config overrides it.

face_match_max_attempts.description: Maximum face-match submissions per session. This value is also copied into generated face-match workflow nodes unless the feature-level config overrides it.

session_expiration_time.description: Seconds before an unfinished session expires. Minimum 1 hour (3600), maximum 4 weeks (2419200).

feature.description: Feature to run. Use the uppercase values shown here.

config.description: Feature-specific settings. For `QUESTIONNAIRE`, include `questionnaire_uuid` with the `questionnaire_id` returned by the questionnaire create endpoint. For `OCR`, `methods` selects which ID Verification methods each country may use (document capture, non-doc lookup against a government or other authoritative source, and digital identity wallets); omit it and every country is document capture only.

label.description: Optional internal label for this workflow node.

ReviewItem.description: One entry in a session's review / activity feed. Status changes carry `previous_status`, `new_status`, `previous_value`, `new_value`, and `changed_fields`; comments carry `comment` and (for Console comments) `mentioned_emails`; the remaining fields are `null` or empty when they do not apply to the activity type.

uuid.description: Unique identifier of this feed entry.

activity_type.description: What kind of activity this entry records. `STATUS_UPDATED` rows come from manual decisions (`PATCH /v3/session/{session_id}/update-status/`) and from entries added via `POST …/reviews/` (which default to this type even when no status is recorded). `COMMENT` rows come from Console reviewers; Console detail-page views are also stored as `COMMENT` rows flagged with `metadata.system_event = "DETAIL_VIEWED"`. The remaining types track data edits, file changes, tags, and AML monitoring activity. STATUS_UPDATED rows are also written by system actors (e.g. AML ongoing monitoring with actor_type SYSTEM, and automatic feature-status updates), not only by the update-status endpoint and manual review posts.

actor_display.description: Human-readable author label, resolved in order: actor's full name → Console account identifier → local part of `actor_email` → `"API Client"` (for `API_KEY` actors) → `"System"` (for `SYSTEM` actors) → `"Unknown"`. Entries created via `POST …/reviews/` always display `"Unknown"` because that endpoint records no actor attribution.

actor_email.description: Email of the Console user who performed the action. `null` for API-key and system actors.

actor_type.description: Who performed the action: an API key, a Console user, or Didit itself (`SYSTEM`, e.g. AML ongoing monitoring). Entries created via `POST …/reviews/` carry the default `CONSOLE_USER` regardless of the caller.

new_status.description: Session status recorded by this entry (for status updates). `null` for comments and data-change entries.

previous_status.description: Status the session had before the change. Populated on `STATUS_UPDATED` entries written by the update-status endpoint; `null` on entries added via `POST …/reviews/`. Also populated on system-written STATUS_UPDATED rows.

comment.description: Free-text note attached to the entry, or `null`.

mentioned_emails.description: Console users `@email`-mentioned in the comment. Always empty for entries created via this API — mention processing is a Console-only feature.

previous_value.description: Snapshot of the changed data before the action, e.g. `{"status": "In Review"}` on a status change. `null` when nothing was changed.

new_value.description: Snapshot of the changed data after the action, e.g. `{"status": "Approved"}`. `null` when nothing was changed.

changed_fields.description: Names of the fields modified by this activity (e.g. `["status"]`). Empty for comments and for entries added via `POST …/reviews/`.

metadata.description: Extra context for system-generated entries. Console detail-page views carry `{"system_event": "DETAIL_VIEWED", "detail_type": "verification"}` so they can be filtered out of notification logic. `null` for ordinary entries.

created_at.description: When the entry was written, ISO 8601 UTC.

QuestionnaireListItem.description: One questionnaire version in the list view.

uuid.description: Per-version UUID. Use as `{questionnaire_uuid}` for get/update/delete and as `questionnaire_uuid` in a workflow's QUESTIONNAIRE feature config.

is_simple_questionnaire.description: True for linear questionnaires created through this API; false for graph-based questionnaires built in the Console.

question_types.description: Uppercase element types of the answerable questions, in creation order (e.g. `SHORT_TEXT`, `MULTIPLE_CHOICE`, `FILE_UPLOAD`). Structural `SECTION_HEADER` and `SEPARATOR` elements are excluded. One entry per question, so values can repeat.

workflow_names.description: Names of workflows using this questionnaire. Currently always `[]` on this endpoint (populated only in the Console listing).

questionnaire_group_id.description: Stable identifier that groups all versions of the same questionnaire.

version.description: Version number within the group, starting at 1.

published_at.description: When this version was published. `null` for drafts.

is_editable.description: True when this version is a `draft`.

SimpleQuestionnaireRequest.description: Create a simple linear questionnaire. The API converts `form_elements` into the internal questionnaire graph.

languages.description: Languages included in every label. Must include `en`.

default_language.description: Default language. Must be included in `languages`.

status.description: Omit this field to create a published questionnaire ready for workflows.

form_elements.description: Questions in the exact order users should see them. Branching and conditional fields are not supported.

SimpleQuestionnaireUpdateRequest.description: Update questionnaire metadata or replace the full linear `form_elements` list.

form_elements.description: If provided, this replaces the full linear question list.

id.description: Optional stable question id. If omitted, the API generates `q1`, `q2`, etc. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores for readability.

element_type.description: Question type. The API accepts these lowercase values and their uppercase equivalents.

label.description: Question label by language code, for example `{ "en": "Source of funds" }`.

options.description: Use for `dropdown`, `single_choice`, and `multiple_choice`. If `value` is omitted, the API generates one from the option label.

validation.description: Optional format validation for `short_text`, `long_text`, or `number`. Enforced while the user fills the field (they cannot proceed until it passes) and re-checked by the API on submission.

pattern.description: Regular expression (ECMA-262 subset) the value must fully match. For `short_text` and `long_text`. Do not add ^/$ anchors; the whole value is matched.

min_length.description: Minimum number of characters. For `short_text` and `long_text`.

max_length.description: Maximum number of characters. For `short_text` and `long_text`.

error_message.description: Translated message shown when validation fails, keyed by language code.

QuestionnaireDetail.description: Full questionnaire detail returned from GET, POST (create) and PATCH (update) endpoints.

questionnaire_id.description: Unique identifier of the questionnaire. Use this id when referencing the questionnaire from a workflow or in subsequent update/delete requests.

graph.description: Graph structure with start_node and nodes map.

sections.description: Questionnaire content grouped into sections (derived from the graph).

questionnaire_group_id.description: Stable identifier that groups all versions of the same questionnaire.

is_editable.description: True when the questionnaire can still be edited in place (draft versions).

didit_internal_id.description: Didit's stable internal UUID for this user.

vendor_data.description: Your unique identifier for this user (passed when creating sessions). This can be null when no vendor identifier was supplied.

display_name.description: Custom display name set by you

full_name.description: Full name extracted from verified documents

effective_name.description: Best available name: display_name if set, otherwise full_name

status.description: Lifecycle status of the user record (NOT a session status). `ACTIVE` is the default, `FLAGGED` marks the user for manual attention, `BLOCKED` prevents new sessions for this `vendor_data`.

portrait_image_url.description: Presigned URL of the user's portrait photo (expires after a few hours)

session_count.description: Total number of verification sessions for this user

issuing_states.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes of issuing countries seen on this user's approved ID documents, e.g. `["USA", "ESP"]`. Empty array when none.

approved_emails.description: Verified email addresses collected from this user's approved sessions, e.g. `["john@example.com"]`.

approved_phones.description: Verified phone numbers collected from this user's approved sessions, e.g. `["+14155551234"]`.

features.description: Aggregated per-feature status across all of this user's sessions. Possible keys: `ID_VERIFICATION`, `NFC`, `LIVENESS`, `FACE_MATCH`, `POA`, `QUESTIONNAIRE`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION`, `PHONE`, `AML`, `IP_ANALYSIS`, `AGE_ESTIMATION`, `DATABASE_VALIDATION`. Possible values: `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, `Not Finished`, `Resub Requested`.

features_list.description: Same data as `features`, as an ordered array of `{feature, status}` objects.

last_session_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent session

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity on this user (session, transaction, status change, data edit, etc.).

UserDetailItem.description: Full user detail. Extends UserListItem with metadata, comments, and updated_at.

metadata.description: Custom metadata JSON you attached to this user. Defaults to `{}`.

tags.description: Tag assignments. NOTE: on detail responses each entry is a tag *link* object (`{uuid, tag: {...}, added_by_email, added_by_name, created_at}`), unlike the flat `{uuid, name, color}` shape used on list responses.

uuid.description: UUID of the tag assignment (not the tag itself).

previous_value.description: Previous field values for PROFILE_UPDATED entries.

new_value.description: New field values for PROFILE_UPDATED entries.

changed_fields.description: Names of the fields changed by a PROFILE_UPDATED entry.

comments.description: Activity log and comments for this user (status changes, profile edits, manual notes).

didit_internal_id.description: Didit's stable internal UUID for this business.

vendor_data.description: Your unique identifier for this business (passed when creating sessions). This can be null when no vendor identifier was supplied.

display_name.description: Custom display name set by you

legal_name.description: Official legal name from registry or manual entry

effective_name.description: Best available name: display_name if set, otherwise legal_name

status.description: Lifecycle status of the business record (NOT a session status). `ACTIVE` is the default, `FLAGGED` marks it for manual attention, `BLOCKED` prevents new sessions for this `vendor_data`.

session_count.description: Total number of verification sessions for this business

features.description: Aggregated per-feature status across all of this business's KYB sessions. Currently the only key is `KYB` (the registry company check status). Possible values: `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, `Not Finished`, `Resub Requested`.

features_list.description: Same data as `features`, as an ordered array of `{feature, status}` objects.

last_session_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent session

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity (status change, session update, etc.)

BusinessDetailItem.description: Full business detail. Extends BusinessListItem with metadata and updated_at.

metadata.description: Custom metadata JSON you attached to this business. Defaults to `{}`.

TransactionDetail.description: Full monitoring record for one transaction, as returned by `GET /v3/transactions/{transaction_id}/` and `POST /v3/transactions/`.

uuid.description: Didit-stable transaction identifier. Use as `{transaction_id}` for follow-up calls.

environment.description: Environment of the application that owns the transaction. A `sandbox` transaction is stored but never evaluated, screened, notified or billed, so its empty `rule_runs` means "not evaluated".

transaction_number.description: Application-scoped sequential transaction number shown in Console (e.g. `4123`).

txn_id.description: The `transaction_id` you supplied at create time (max 128 chars). Unique per application.

txn_date.description: When the transaction occurred (from `transaction_at`; defaults to submission time).

zone_id.description: IANA time zone identifier provided at create time.

transaction_type.description: Top-level category as stored: `finance`, `kyc`, `travelRule`, `userPlatformEvent`, `gamblingBet`, `gamblingLimitChange`, `gamblingBonusChange`, `auditTrailEvent`. Note multi-word values are echoed back in camelCase even when submitted in snake_case.

action_type.description: Sub-type within the category (e.g. `deposit`, `withdrawal`, `transfer`). Defaults to the category when not supplied.

direction.description: Direction relative to the subject. Stored uppercase regardless of the casing submitted (`in`/`out`/`inbound`/`outbound` are accepted on input).

status.description: Current monitoring verdict. Transactions are created `APPROVED`; rules may flip them to `IN_REVIEW`/`DECLINED` synchronously.

source.description: How the record originated: `LIVE` for transactions submitted through the API or SDK, `IMPORTED` for transactions loaded through the console import.

amount.description: Transaction amount as a decimal string with trailing zeros stripped (e.g. `"1500"`, `"0.5"`, `"0.123456789012345678"`). Up to 18 decimal places.

currency.description: Currency code of `amount`. Any ISO 4217 alphabetic code is accepted (e.g. `EUR`, `USD`, `NGN`), as is a crypto asset symbol (e.g. `BTC`). Prefer a currently-circulating code. Not every accepted code has an exchange rate: when none is available for the code (for example the ISO accounting unit `XSU`, or a crypto symbol Didit does not price), automatic conversion fails and `preferred_currency_amount` is returned null unless the request supplied a pre-converted `amount_in_default_currency`.

amount_in_default_currency.description: Pre-converted amount you supplied, as a decimal string with trailing zeros stripped.

preferred_currency_amount.description: `amount` converted to the application's preferred currency, when available.

payment_details.description: Free-text payment reference or memo from the submission.

payment_txn_id.description: External payment system reference (e.g. blockchain transaction hash) from `payment_reference_id`.

score.description: Risk score accumulated by rules (typically 0–100). Higher = riskier.

severity.description: Categorical risk severity set by rules/providers (`UNKNOWN`, `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL`). `null` until something sets it.

vendor_data.description: Convenience copy of the applicant's `vendor_data`.

metadata.description: Snapshot of the `subject` and `counterparty` payloads as submitted at create time.

props.description: The `custom_properties` you supplied at create time. Each key is addressable in rule conditions as `custom_values.<key>`.

source.description: Whether the tag is a Didit preset or a custom tag.

tags.description: Tags attached to the transaction (manually or by rules).

role.description: Party role. The create endpoint assigns `APPLICANT` (the subject) and `COUNTERPARTY`.

kind.description: `USER`/`BUSINESS` parties link back to a Didit-owned entity via `vendor_data`. `EXTERNAL` parties have no Didit entity behind them.

vendor_data.description: Your internal user/business identifier.

country_code.description: Country code from the submitted `address.country` (typically ISO 3166-1 alpha-3).

dob.description: Date of birth from the submitted `date_of_birth`.

address.description: Address object as submitted. `{}` when omitted.

institution_info.description: Institution details as submitted. `{}` when omitted.

device.description: Normalized device context, including server-side IP enrichment under network_context (geolocation, VPN/data-center flags) when an IP was provided.

persistent_device_id.description: Stable cross-session device identifier (v2 fingerprint schema).

user_agent.description: Browser or app user agent string.

platform.description: Platform identifier (web, ios, android, macos, windows, linux).

os_family.description: Operating system family (e.g. iOS, Android, Windows).

session_id.description: Session identifier (stored in metadata).

network_context.description: Network context with IP address and geo-location.

ip_country_code.description: Geo-resolved country of the IP (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3).

external_party_snapshot.description: Frozen copy of the party data for `EXTERNAL` parties. `null` while the party is linked to a Didit user or business.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 over `type:account_id:issuing_country` — stable identifier to correlate reuse of the same instrument.

account_id.description: Account identifier (IBAN, wallet address, card token, …).

vendor_data.description: Your identifier for the owning user/business.

role.description: How this method was used in the transaction. The create endpoint assigns `SOURCE`/`DESTINATION` from the direction (outbound: subject = SOURCE; inbound: subject = DESTINATION).

payment_methods.description: Payment methods linked to the transaction.

documents.description: Files attached to the transaction from the console. `[]` when none.

file_url.description: Short-lived signed download URL; fetch it when needed rather than storing it.

activities.description: Activity log entries (creation, notes, manual reviews, status changes).

alerts.description: Alerts raised by rules and providers.

rule.description: UUID of the rule that ran.

matched.description: Whether the rule's conditions matched this transaction. A run is recorded only for matched rules, so live evaluations always carry `true`.

is_test.description: True when the rule ran in TEST mode (no effect on status/score).

score_delta.description: Score added by this rule's `add_score` actions.

status_target.description: Status set by a `change_status` action, if any.

action_summary.description: Summary of the actions the rule executed, joined with `; ` (e.g. `score +30; change_status:IN_REVIEW; add_tag:high_risk_country`). Parts: `score +N`, `change_status:<STATUS>`, `add_tag:<name>`, `add_note`, `add_to_list`, `open_case`. `null` when the rule executed no action.

metadata.description: Evaluation detail: `scope_match`, `conditions[]` and `aggregations[]`. Each condition entry carries `field`, `operator`, `expected_value`, the `current_value` read from the transaction, `matched`, `group_index` and `group_logic`. Each aggregation entry (velocity / count / sum) carries `metric`, `field`, `operator`, `expected_value`, the `computed_value` the aggregate evaluated to, `window`, `filters`, `matched` and `sample_references`; deferred async aggregations have `computed_value: null` and `deferred: true`.

rule_runs.description: Per-rule execution results — which rule fired, with what score impact.

provider_results.description: Raw provider payloads (AML screening, blockchain analytics, etc.).

travel_rule.description: Travel Rule transfer or check. Populated when `travel_rule_details` was submitted, and also when Travel Rule is enabled and the transaction was created with `transaction_category: travelRule` (Didit initiates the exchange itself, even without `travel_rule_details`). `null` when no transfer or check exists.

network_snapshot.description: Graph snapshot of related transactions/parties used by the rules engine. Either the `network_snapshot` submitted with the transaction or the graph Didit builds from a successful AML wallet screening (which replaces a submitted one). `null` when neither exists.

remediation.description: Remediation session offered to the user when re-verification is required. Superseded by `action_required`, which is the canonical block; kept for backward compatibility.

action_required.description: Pending end-user action required to complete this transaction, or null when there is none. The Didit SDKs auto-launch the action by default and refresh the transaction when it finishes. Two variants, discriminated by `type`: `verification_session` (a hosted verification session created by a rule action) and `wallet_ownership` (a wallet-ownership widget session auto-minted for a Travel Rule transfer that needs proof of wallet control, gated by the `auto_wallet_verification` Travel Rule setting). When both could apply, `wallet_ownership` takes precedence because it blocks the Travel Rule exchange.

url.description: Hosted verification URL to open for the end user.

session_id.description: Verification session id.

session_token.description: Session token, used by the mobile SDKs to launch the flow natively.
