cost_breakdown.description: Cost of this transaction: `total_price` and `items`, one per charge, each with `usage_type`, `price`, `details` and `created_at`. A re-screen of the same transaction is a new item.

is_enabled.description: Whether the managed Travel Rule negotiation flow is active for outbound `travelRule` transactions on this application.

jurisdiction.description: Your VASP's operating jurisdiction code. Default `"EU"`.

name_matching_strictness.description: How strictly beneficiary names must match before a transfer can reach COMPLETED.

confirmation_timeout_hours.description: Hours an AWAITING_COUNTERPARTY transfer may remain unconfirmed before the periodic sweeper expires it. Default 48.

timeout_outcome.description: What happens to the underlying transaction when a transfer expires. Default HOLD.

threshold_amount.description: Decimal string. Minimum transfer amount that triggers a managed exchange; transfers below it resolve straight to NOT_APPLICABLE. Defaults to "0.00" (EU TFR applies no minimum amount).

legal_name.description: Your VASP's legal name. Required (non-blank) to set is_enabled to true.

lei.description: Your Legal Entity Identifier, surfaced in the VASP directory.

compliance_email.description: Compliance contact email for your VASP profile.

is_discoverable.description: Whether your VASP profile appears in GET /v3/travel-rule/vasps/ search results and can be reached on the INTERNAL rail. Default true.

inbound_auto_accept.description: When true, inbound transfers whose beneficiary wallet is a verified address-book entry with a matching name are accepted automatically, without a manual review step. Default false.

allow_self_declaration.description: When true, the wallet-ownership widget offers self-declaration as a fallback proof method. Default false.

allow_screenshot_proof.description: When true, the wallet-ownership widget offers screenshot upload as an ownership evidence method. Default true.

auto_wallet_verification.description: When true, submitting an outbound Travel Rule transfer that needs end-user proof of wallet control auto-mints a wallet-ownership widget session bound to the transaction and exposes it in the transaction's action_required block. Default true.

vasp_attribution_enabled.description: When true, an outbound Travel Rule transfer that no rail can route is attributed through blockchain analytics: the destination wallet is resolved to its owning VASP, the entity is recorded on the transfer and in the VASP directory, and the rails are re-run once with the attributed name. Default true.

travel_address.description: Read-only. Your VASP's own travel address - the encoded inbound TRP inquiry endpoint other VASPs use to reach you. Populated once your VASP profile is complete.

TravelRuleTransferDetail.description: Full transfer object returned by the ownership-confirmation and finish/cancel endpoints. originator_data/beneficiary_data are omitted while PII is masked (see description).

TravelRuleTransferPatchRequest.description: Provide exactly one of: payment_txn_id (finish), action=cancel, or action=resend.

is_didit_customer.description: true for discoverable Didit applications (dd_status is always COMPLETED, dd_score always 0 for these); false for internal counterparty-registry rows, which carry a real due-diligence status and score.

dd_score_breakdown.description: Per-component contributions to dd_score (licensing/registry, sanctions/PEP, jurisdiction risk, on-chain analytics risk), all derived from checks Didit runs in-house. Empty for Didit-customer rows.

dd_assessed_at.description: When the due-diligence assessment last ran. Null for Didit-customer rows.

beneficiary_name.description: Required in practice for decision=accept; run through the originator's name_matching_strictness policy.

chain.description: Chain the deposit settled on, e.g. "ethereum".

txid.description: On-chain transaction hash. Deduped together with wallet_address.

wallet_address.description: The destination wallet you received the deposit on.

amount.description: Deposit amount as a decimal string.

originator_data.description: IVMS-101 originator payload from the sending VASP, if known.

originating_vasp.description: Optional description of the sending VASP.

travel_address.description: Travel address that lets Didit reach the sender on the TRP rail.

transaction_id.description: Didit transaction UUID for the inbound deposit.

txn_id.description: Didit-generated txn_id for the sunrise transaction.

created.description: true when a new transaction was minted (HTTP 201); false when an existing unclaimed deposit was reused (HTTP 200).

holder_name.description: Name of the wallet holder, used for the beneficiary name match.

vendor_data.description: Your internal identifier for the holder, carried onto the created address-book entry.

transaction_id.description: Optional. Didit transaction UUID of a Travel Rule transfer to advance when the proof verifies.

satoshi_deposit_address.description: Optional. A deposit address you control; supplying it enables the SATOSHI_TEST proof method.

callback_url.description: Optional. Where the widget returns the customer after completion.

expires_in_minutes.description: Optional. Lifetime of the minted link, in minutes. Automatically extended to cover the Satoshi test window when SATOSHI_TEST is offered.

token.description: Opaque session token embedded in the widget URL.

url.description: The hosted wallet-ownership widget URL. Open it verbatim in the system browser (never inside a mobile SDK webview).

vasp_name.description: Legal name from your VASP profile, shown to the customer in the widget. Empty when no profile exists.

allowed_methods.description: Proof methods available for this session. MESSAGE_SIGNING requires a supported chain family, SATOSHI_TEST requires a satoshi_deposit_address on the session, SCREENSHOT requires the allow_screenshot_proof setting, and SELF_DECLARATION requires the allow_self_declaration setting.

transfer_status.description: Status of the linked Travel Rule transfer. Null when the session was minted without a transaction_id.

callback_url.description: Where the widget returns the customer after completion. Empty when not set.

completed_at.description: Non-null once a proof has been verified.

customization.description: The application's whitelabel customization (colors, logo, font family) when white label is enabled - the widget renders with the same branding as the verification flow. Null otherwise.

status.description: PENDING on a SATOSHI_TEST proof means the deposit has been seen on-chain but has not yet reached enough confirmations; a background job automatically rechecks it and moves it to VERIFIED once it confirms, with no resubmission needed. REJECTED means a genuinely wrong deposit was submitted (absent, wrong sender, or wrong amount). EXPIRED means the proof's own test window closed before a valid deposit was seen.

deposit_address.description: Deposit address the customer must send the Satoshi test amount to. Present only on a SATOSHI_TEST proof.

expected_amount.description: Exact on-chain amount, in the deposit's native currency, the Satoshi test deposit must match. Present only on a SATOSHI_TEST proof.

expires_at.description: Deadline for this proof's own Satoshi test window. Present only on a SATOSHI_TEST proof; the widget session's own expires_at is extended to cover it when SATOSHI_TEST is offered.

challenge.description: Didit-issued message the customer signs with their wallet. Present only on a MESSAGE_SIGNING proof.

CaseSubject.description: The single user or business the case is anchored to.

CaseContentConfig.description: The six togglable sections that drive which tabs and fields appear on the case page. Unknown sections or keys are rejected.

optional.description: When true, a case can be resolved with incomplete checklist items.

linked_entity_summary.description: session_id/session_number/status for session and business_session links; uuid/txn_id/status for transaction links.

content_config.description: The six togglable sections that drive which tabs and fields appear on the case page. Unknown sections or keys are rejected.

optional.description: When true, a case can be resolved with incomplete checklist items.

creation_sources.description: Connectors currently routing new cases into this blueprint.

receives_escalation_from.description: Other blueprints whose Escalation target points at this one.

pending_resolution.description: Set only while a 4-eyes resolution is staged on the checker blueprint, awaiting approve or reject-approval.

field_config.description: Reusable goAML header defaults. Template-level obligatory fields: rentity_id, submission_code, and currency_code_local (3-letter). Optional: enabled_fields (which optional report blocks to include) plus reporting_person, location, reason, and action defaults. Per-filing header fields (action, submission_date, transactions, jurisdiction) are enforced when the report is validated or finalized, not on the template.

report_code.description: goAML report code derived from report_type, e.g. STR, CTR, BCR.

rentity_id.description: Reporting entity ID issued by the FIU.

validation_errors.description: Result of the most recent validation; each entry is a {field, message} object.

field.description: Transaction field path to evaluate. Core fields: amount, currency, direction, action_type, score, severity, transaction_type, payment_details, preferred_currency_amount (falls back to amount_in_default_currency), default_currency_code, subject_country, counterparty_country, subject_vendor_data, counterparty_vendor_data, subject_device_fingerprint, counterparty_device_fingerprint, subject_browser_family, subject_browser_version, subject_platform, subject_accept_language, subject_session_age_ms, subject_ip_country, counterparty_ip_country, subject_ip_address, counterparty_ip_address, subject_payment_method_type, subject_payment_method_country, subject_payment_method_fingerprint, subject_payment_method_account_id (and the counterparty_payment_method_* equivalents), travel_rule_status, travel_rule_required, travel_rule_obligations_count, subject_days_since_previous_transaction, tags, and custom_values.<key> for any key submitted in custom_properties on transaction create. Country-code fields accept ISO-2 or ISO-3; both sides are normalized to ISO-3 before comparison.

operator.description: Comparison operator. in/not_in test membership (value may be a list or a single scalar). contains/not_contains are case-insensitive substring checks against a string value. contains_any takes a list of strings and matches when any is a case-insensitive substring of the field value. regex matches the value pattern against the field. fuzzy_match compares against the value string with the required `score` threshold (0-100). gt/gte/lt/lte never match when either side is missing. exists/is_not_empty/is_not_null (aliases) and not_exists/is_empty/is_null (aliases) are presence checks that ignore `value`.

value.description: Comparison value. Its shape depends on the operator and value_type; omit for the presence-check operators.

value_type.description: Optional value interpretation. `list`: value is a List UUID and the list's entries become the comparison value. `field`: value is another field path, compared field-to-field. `relative_date`: value is a relative-date object, e.g. {"direction": "past", "unit": "days", "amount": 30}.

score.description: Required when operator is fuzzy_match: the 0-100 similarity threshold.

group_index.description: Optional grouped logic. When any condition carries group_index, conditions sharing an index form a group and grouped evaluation replaces evaluation_mode.

group_logic.description: How conditions combine WITHIN a group.

groups_logic.description: How group outcomes combine ACROSS groups. Read from the first condition.

TransactionRuleCondition.description: A condition reads only the transaction being evaluated - it never filters the aggregation window.

metric.description: How the matching historical transactions are aggregated. unique_count is accepted as an alias of distinct_count.

field.description: Field aggregated by sum/max/min/avg/distinct_count. Ignored for count.

operator.description: Comparison applied to the computed metric.

value.description: Threshold the computed metric is compared against.

window.description: Look-back window ending at the transaction's txn_date: <N>m (MINUTES, not months), <N>h (hours) or <N>d (days), e.g. 30m, 24h, 7d, 30d.

filters.description: Narrows which historical transactions are aggregated. Keys are field paths from the condition field catalog; a value of "__current__" resolves to the same field's value on the transaction being evaluated (e.g. {"subject_vendor_data": "__current__"} scopes the window to the same subject), and a list value means membership. Filters compare by equality or membership ONLY - there is no lt/gte filter, so a range such as "historical transactions under 10,000" cannot be expressed here. Put the range on the metric instead (metric max with operator lt keeps every transaction in the window below the threshold).

TransactionRuleAggregation.description: Velocity check over the application's historical transactions inside the window. Every aggregation entry must match for the rule to match, regardless of evaluation_mode. An aggregation constrains only the window; the transaction being evaluated is constrained by scope and conditions, so repeat direction, currency or transaction_type on both halves when the rule promises them.

transaction_types.description: Restrict to transaction types, e.g. finance, kyc, travel_rule, user_event. Empty or missing = no restriction.

directions.description: Restrict to transaction directions (case-insensitive on write).

action_types.description: Restrict to your action_type values, e.g. withdrawal, deposit.

TransactionRuleScope.description: Which transactions the rule applies to. Only these three keys are accepted.

value.description: Points added to the transaction's risk score. May be negative.

oneOf.description: Add points to the transaction's cumulative risk score; the total decides the status via the application's review/decline thresholds.

value.description: Status to set immediately, regardless of score. Alias key: status.

workflow_id.description: REQUIRED when value is AWAITING_USER: the verification workflow the subject is asked to complete. Alias key: remediation_workflow_id. Didit creates a hosted remediation session for the subject when the rule fires.

oneOf.description: Directly set the transaction status. DECLINED always wins across matched rules.

tag_name.description: Tag name to attach; created on first use (stored uppercased). Provide tag_uuid or tag_name.

tag_color.description: Hex color used when tag_name creates a new tag, e.g. #007AFE.

oneOf.description: Attach an application tag to the matched transaction.

note.description: Note text attached to the transaction (author: Rule Engine). Alias key: value.

oneOf.description: Attach an automated analyst note to the matched transaction.

list_id.description: List to add the subject's vendor_data to.

oneOf.description: Add the subject's vendor_data to a blocklist, allowlist or custom list.

blueprint.description: Case blueprint UUID; defaults to the application's default blueprint.

grouping.description: Whether repeat matches join one case per applicant or one per rule+applicant.

attach_matched_transaction.description: Attach the matched transaction to the case.

oneOf.description: Open (or add to) an investigation case. Only the first open_case action on a rule is applied.

TransactionRuleAction.description: One rule action. A rule can carry several; all are applied together when it matches. Rules in TEST mode record what they would have done without applying any action.

title.description: Rule name. Unique per application among non-deleted rules; duplicates return 400.

category.description: Risk theme used for grouping and reporting, e.g. finance, aml_ctf, anomaly_detection, fatf, device_intelligence, crypto_monitoring, travel_rule, responsible_gaming, e_commerce.

mode.description: ACTIVE evaluates live. TEST evaluates and records rule runs but never touches score or status - the recommended starting mode. DISABLED is skipped.

evaluation_mode.description: Whether every condition must match (ALL) or at least one (ANY). Ignored when conditions use group_index.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata stored on the rule.

library_key.description: Stable library identifier; null for custom rules.

run_count.description: How many transactions matched this rule.

TransactionRuleBacktestRequest.description: Hypothetical rule configuration to evaluate against recent transactions. Read-only and free: nothing is created or modified. Send the same conditions, aggregation, evaluation_mode AND scope as the rule you intend to activate. Omitted conditions, aggregation and scope add no constraints of their own; dropping scope can include directions or transaction types the saved rule skips. Omitted evaluation_mode defaults to ALL (which can reduce matches for an ANY rule), and omitted period_days defaults to 90 days, not unlimited history.

matched.description: Transactions the configuration would have matched.

affected_entities.description: Distinct subjects (by vendor_data) among the matches.

bundle.description: Functional family, e.g. finance, aml_ctf, crypto_monitoring, travel_rule, responsible_gaming.

is_installed.description: Whether this preset is currently installed on the application.

library_keys.description: Specific presets to install or uninstall.

bundle.description: Install or uninstall every preset in this bundle instead.

installed_library_keys.description: POST (install) only: presets installed by this call.

uninstalled_count.description: DELETE (uninstall) only: presets removed by this call.

risk_score.description: Normalised 0-100 risk score. Higher means greater exposure to risky entities. Merkle Science grades an address 0-5, which maps to 0, 15, 35, 55, 75 or 95.

severity.description: Risk bucket derived from `risk_score`: `0-9` UNKNOWN, `10-39` LOW, `40-69` MEDIUM, `70-89` HIGH, `90-100` CRITICAL. `UNKNOWN` is the lowest band, not a separate no-data state: `risk_score` 0 (the common clean-address case) means no adverse assessment, while a non-zero score in the 1-9 range is a real but sub-LOW signal - read the `risk_score`, not just the band. Never treat `UNKNOWN` as an affirmative low-risk or clear rating; do not display it as a pass.

status.description: Screening outcome status.

summary.description: Human-readable summary of the screening result.

transaction_hash.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always `null` on a wallet screening result.

block_timestamp.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always `null` on a wallet screening result.

total_value_usd.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always `null` on a wallet screening result.

fee_usd.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always `null` on a wallet screening result.

sender_rows.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always empty on a wallet screening result.

receiver_rows.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always empty on a wallet screening result.

transaction_flows.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always empty on a wallet screening result.

transaction_flows_status.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always `null` on a wallet screening result.

transaction_flows_error.description: Transaction screening field, shared with the result shape. Always `null` on a wallet screening result.

source_of_funds.description: Where the address received funds from, attributed by entity. Each entry is an exposure breakdown.

percentage.description: Share of the direction's total exposure, 0-100.

amount_usd.description: USD value attributed to this entity.

entity_name.description: Name of the attributed entity, for example an exchange, a mixer or a sanctioned group.

entity_subtype.description: More granular subtype (e.g. `Mandatory KYC and AML`, `OFAC`, `Yield Aggregator`).

hops.description: Number of hops to the entity (1 for a direct counterparty), when the provider reports one. Always `null` for Merkle Science, which reports only whether exposure is direct or indirect: use `exposure_type`.

description.description: `entity_type / entity_subtype`, as the provider labels the entity.

exposure_direction.description: Whether the funds came from (`incoming`) or went to (`outgoing`) this entity.

provider_entity_id.description: The provider's own identifier for the entity.

country.description: Primary ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the entity. Empty or `null` when the provider does not know it.

raw_amount.description: Amount in the asset's own unit, when the provider reports it.

raw_currency.description: Unit of `raw_amount`, when the provider reports it.

destination_of_funds.description: Where the address sent funds to, attributed by entity. Same item shape as `source_of_funds` with `exposure_direction` = `outgoing`.

percentage.description: Share of the direction's total exposure, 0-100.

amount_usd.description: USD value attributed to this entity.

entity_name.description: Name of the attributed entity, for example an exchange, a mixer or a sanctioned group.

entity_subtype.description: More granular subtype (e.g. `Mandatory KYC and AML`, `OFAC`, `Yield Aggregator`).

hops.description: Number of hops to the entity (1 for a direct counterparty), when the provider reports one. Always `null` for Merkle Science, which reports only whether exposure is direct or indirect: use `exposure_type`.

description.description: `entity_type / entity_subtype`, as the provider labels the entity.

exposure_direction.description: Whether the funds came from (`incoming`) or went to (`outgoing`) this entity.

provider_entity_id.description: The provider's own identifier for the entity.

country.description: Primary ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the entity. Empty or `null` when the provider does not know it.

raw_amount.description: Amount in the asset's own unit, when the provider reports it.

raw_currency.description: Unit of `raw_amount`, when the provider reports it.

counterparty_connections.description: Entities the provider attributes the screened address to. For Merkle Science these come from the address's own owner and user tags, so the same entity can appear twice, and they carry no fund flows: `received_usd`, `sent_usd`, `received_hops` and `sent_hops` are `null` and `percentage` is 0. Do not route on `risk_level` or `is_direct` here: use `sanctions_hit`, `dominant_risk_category` and `risk_factors[].is_high_risk` for the verdict, and `exposure_type` in `source_of_funds`/`destination_of_funds` for directness.

risk_level.description: Lowercase and provider-dependent. For Merkle Science it is the address's own 0-5 risk grade (`no_risk`, `low`, `medium_low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`), raised to `high` when the entity's category is high risk; it is not a separate grade of the entity.

categories.description: Normalised risk categories of the entity.

received_usd.description: USD received from the entity, when the provider reports it.

sent_usd.description: USD sent to the entity, when the provider reports it.

received_hops.description: Hops to the entity on the receiving side, when the provider reports them.

sent_hops.description: Hops to the entity on the sending side, when the provider reports them.

percentage.description: Share of the address's exposure, when the provider reports it; otherwise 0.

is_direct.description: Always `true` for Merkle Science, whose connections are attributions rather than counterparties.

country.description: Country of the entity, when known.

provider_entity_id.description: The provider's own identifier for the entity.

network_nodes.description: Exposure graph nodes for transaction screening. Empty on a wallet screening result.

network_edges.description: Exposure graph edges for transaction screening. Empty on a wallet screening result.

sanctions_hit.description: True if the address has direct or indirect sanctions exposure.

pep_counterparty.description: Politically exposed person exposure. `null` when no PEP finding is available, which is every result today because no provider reports one; `false` only for an explicit negative screening result. Do not read `null` as a completed PEP check.

dominant_risk_category.description: Highest-weighted high-risk category, or `null` when none is dominant (e.g. `sanctioned`, `mixer`, `stolen_funds`).

risk_factors.description: Ranked explanation of `risk_score`: what produced this verdict. Providers grade an address on their own model and return only a verdict (Merkle Science returns an integer 0-5), so the score alone is not actionable. Ordered high-risk first, then by the value that moved through each driver, capped at the five strongest; `source_of_funds` and `destination_of_funds` always carry the complete breakdown. A high `risk_score` with no `is_high_risk` entry means the provider reported no sanctions or attributed-entity match and graded the address purely on its own exposure model - `summary` states this explicitly.

source.description: `attribution` is what the provider says the address itself is (its own tag or cluster); `exposure` is where its funds actually moved.

category.description: Normalised risk category, same vocabulary as the exposure breakdown.

label.description: The provider's own wording for the driver (e.g. `Gambling / Crypto only`), which is what you would also see in the provider's console.

entity_name.description: Attributed entity behind the driver, for example a gambling site or an exchange.

direction.description: Direction of the fund flow, `attribution` when the driver is the address's own tag, or `unknown` when the provider did not report a direction.

exposure_type.description: `direct` (1 hop) or `indirect` (multi-hop), `attribution` for the address's own tag, or `unknown` when the provider did not state how many hops away the counterparty is. Treat `unknown` as unclassified, not as `direct`.

amount_usd.description: USD value attributed to this driver.

percentage.description: Share of the address's TOTAL screened volume, both directions combined - unlike `percentage` inside `source_of_funds`/`destination_of_funds`, which is normalised per direction. Comparable and summable across the whole list.

is_high_risk.description: Whether the category is one Didit treats as high risk (`sanctioned`, `mixer`, `stolen_funds`, `ransomware`, `scam`, `darknet_market`, `terrorist_financing`, `child_exploitation`, `hacked_exchange`, `high_risk_exchange`, `seized_funds`).

description.description: One-line rendering of the driver, e.g. `9.01% indirect outgoing exposure to Gambling / Crypto only (Example Gambling)`.

raw_response.description: The provider's own payload. Its shape is provider-specific and can change without notice: read the normalised fields instead of parsing it.

report_signature.description: Opaque HMAC-SHA256 signature over this exact result, scoped to your application. Not meaningful on its own — repost the full response body, unmodified and including this field, to `POST /v3/wallet-screening/pdf/` to render it as a PDF. The PDF endpoint rejects the request with `400` if `report_signature` is missing or if any signed field (e.g. `risk_score`, `severity`, `sanctions_hit`) was edited before repost.

score.description: Risk score, 0-100.

band.description: Band the score renders as. high >= 70, medium >= 40, otherwise low.

bar.description: Normalized 0-1 value for rendering a risk bar.

color.description: Null for guard tags, whose color token the renderer owns.

source.description: Where the tag came from: a tag on the user/business, a tag on a session in this network, a tag on a transaction a party belongs to, or a signal guard condition (e.g. hub, datacenter IP).

category.description: customer for customer-defined tags, quality for signal-quality guard tags. Null when not applicable.

network_id.description: Human-readable per-organization sequential id, e.g. N-0001.

status.description: Network lifecycle status. Distinct from the per-applicant outcome_status inside a network (approved/in_review/declined/not_completed).

pattern_types.description: The clustering patterns detected in this network.

signal_types.description: The distinct signal types present in this network.

member_counts.description: Counts of members by category (e.g. total, per outcome_status).

signal_coverage.description: Per signal_type coverage of this network's members.

stats.description: Aggregate stats for the network (e.g. member totals).

fraud_tags.description: Fraud-pattern tags surfaced on the network.

notes_count.description: Number of private analyst notes in this investigation.

NetworkGraphNode.description: A subject node or a signal node, distinguished by kind. Subject nodes (kind: vendor_user | vendor_business | transaction_party) carry id, kind, subject, node_status (approved | in_review | declined | not_completed), and tags. Signal nodes (kind: signal) carry id, kind, uuid, signal_type, subject_count, coverage, is_hub, is_datacenter_ip, is_high_collision_device, node_status (signal_active | signal_guarded), tags, risk_evidence, first_seen_at, and last_seen_at.

depth.description: Effective depth applied, or null when unbounded (depth=all).

truncated.description: True if the neighborhood was cut off by depth.

subject.description: The vendor_user, vendor_business, or transaction_party this member represents.

node_status.description: For a member row this is always one of the subject-outcome values: approved, in_review, declined, or not_completed.

is_hub.description: True when this signal links an unusually large number of subjects.

event_type.description: e.g. network_detected, signal_observed, network_in_review, network_resolved, network_dismissed.

convergence_count.description: Number of distinct address/location points members converge on.

KYBRegistryAddress.description: An address the registry states, in the same shape for every country and registry source. Every key is always present; a part the registry does not publish is null.

type.description: Address type in lower case: `registered` for the registered office; other types as the registry names them (for example `postal`, `office`). `null` when the registry does not say what the address is.

address.description: The full address as one line. Always present on every address.

description.description: The registry's own label for the address, when it gives one.

KYBRegistryIndustry.description: An activity the registry classifies the company under, in the same shape for every country and registry source.

code.description: Activity code as the registry prints it (for example `73110`).

description.description: Activity label, when the registry publishes one.

scheme.description: Classification system, one name per system whichever source reported it: `UK SIC 2007`, `US SIC`, `NACE Rev. 2`, `NACE Rev. 2.1`, `NAF Rev. 2`, `CNAE`, `SBI`, `NOGA 2008`, `CAE Rev. 4`, `Canada SIC 1977`; other national systems keep the registry's own name. Null when the registry does not name the system.

is_primary.description: True for the company's main activity. Exactly one entry is primary when the list is not empty.

KYBRegistryShareholding.description: What an owner holds, in the same shape for every country and registry source. Null when the registry states no holding. A band (for example a UK PSC's 25-50%) is not a stake: `percentage` is null and the band stays in `ownership_min_shares` / `ownership_max_shares`.

share_class.description: Share class or type as the registry names it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of the values below.

percentage.description: Exact stake in percent, to four decimal places.

KYBRegistryOwnership.description: The outcome of the ownership (Shareholders / UBO) tier, in the same shape for every country and registry source.

status.description: `delivered` when the registry published ownership; `unavailable` when it did not (see `unavailable_reason`); `pending` while the registry is still fetching it; `not_requested` for the Basic tier.

tier_delivered.description: The tier the registry delivered (and that is billed). A UBO request answered with direct shareholders only is `shareholders`.

unavailable_reason.description: Why a requested ownership tier was not delivered. Null unless `status` is `unavailable` or `pending`.

direct_ownership_complete.description: True when the direct shareholders' stated stakes add up to 100% (within one percentage point of rounding); false when they do not; null when ownership was not delivered or a stake is not stated.

unresolved.description: Parts of the ownership chain the registry could not resolve, for example no group structure on record above the direct owners.

value.description: The identifier value, in any customary format.

issuer.description: Optional issuing authority or sub-national issuer, when the country alone is not unique.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Your application's API key, from Developers -> API keys in the Business Console. The primary key has full access. A named key can be scoped: none, read or write per resource, limited to some workflows or to approved sessions, to a list of IP addresses, and to an expiry date. 401 means the key is missing, wrong, revoked or expired; 403 means the key has no access to this resource or action, or the request came from an address outside its IP list; 404 on a session route means the session is outside the key's workflows or statuses. A key without media access receives image, video and PDF URLs as null, and a key without sessions write receives session links and tokens as null. See https://docs.didit.me/console/api-keys.

TransactionTokenAuth.name: X-Transaction-Token
TransactionTokenAuth.description: Short-lived scoped token minted by your backend via POST /v3/transactions/sdk-token/. Used by the Didit SDKs on the device-facing /v1/transactions/ endpoints.

SessionTokenAuth.name: Session-Token
SessionTokenAuth.description: Short-lived token returned in the `session_token` field of POST /v3/session/. Used by the hosted verification flow (and custom sandbox UIs) to call session-scoped endpoints on behalf of the verifying user, without your server-side API key.
